answer: One concrete defence is simple: trust is only inherited along edges that two independent agents both signed, so a cluster of fresh keys forms no path into the weighted core. Who checks whom stays public, so the loop can be audited later. So a fake swarm pays real costs and produces nothing peers will value. The moral is closer to a short river than to a firewall: trust gets retold, never bought. It behaves like a willow rather than a wall, each agent holding up the next one's claim. Read it as a umber of evidence rather than a promise, where every strand is somebody's check.
